messages.subject: Distinguishing groups within facets
parts:
Hi,


I am using a code like the following to plot p-values for different
groups across a number of covariates:

library(ggplot2)

y<- rep(c("a","b","c","d"),2)
p<- abs(rnorm(n=8))
group<-rep(c("1","2"),4)
df <- data.frame(p, y, group)

ggplot(data = df, mapping = aes(x = p, y= y
))+ geom_point(mapping=aes(y=y, x=p), stat="identity")

I want the covariates to be on the y-axis and the p-values on the x-
axis. The problem is that there are different subsets ("groups" in
this data) for each combination of y and x --as reflected in different
dots located on the same rows. Therefore, I would like the p-values to
be plotted on separate rows. While faceting would offer a solution, it
is not what I am looking for. I want the different groups to be
identified within the same facet/panel (I am also avoiding colors
because I am using that for something else). The end result would have
the y labels spanning over different groups on the left hand side,
something like the following --with the plot on the right of course:
y group

a 1
2
b 1
2
c 1
2
d 1
2

Any help would be very much appreciated.

Luis

messages.author: 68b661fcb57b94a9
messages.subject: Re: Distinguishing groups within facets
parts:
Hi Luis,


I'd give, "y" a different name in order to facilitate the following:

y_group<- rep(c("a","a","b","b","c","c","d","d"))

df <- data.frame(p, y_group, group)
df$group<-factor(df$group,levels=c("2","1"))


I know you said you didn't want to use faceting, but does this not give you what you need?
 
ggplot(df, aes(p, group))+geom_point(stat="identity")+facet_grid(y_group~.)


Adam
